# Feature catalog

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_feature_catalog.py from the feature registry. Do not edit by hand: run `make feature-catalog`. -->

Every feature uses only candles up to and including day *t* (its close is known at the
end of day *t*). `lookback` = earlier rows needed; the first `lookback` rows are
warm-up and are dropped by the builder, never filled. Every feature passes the
truncation test (`backend/tests/unit/test_feature_leakage.py`).

## Feature sets

| version | features | warm-up rows | code hash |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v1` | 12 | 49 | `92c21d11b1a2` |

## calendar

Source: [`backend/src/marketlens/features/calendar.py`](../backend/src/marketlens/features/calendar.py)

Calendar effects. Bitcoin trades 7 days a week, so weekends are real trading days.

Possible signal: weekend liquidity is thinner (fewer institutions, closed traditional markets)
and some weekly patterns have been reported. Known in advance, so trivially leakage-free.
Encoded as an integer; models that need it categorical should one-hot it in their pipeline.

| feature | lookback | in sets | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day_of_week` | 0 | v1 | UTC day of week of the candle: 0 = Monday ... 6 = Sunday |

## momentum

Source: [`backend/src/marketlens/features/momentum.py`](../backend/src/marketlens/features/momentum.py)

Distance of the close from its trailing simple moving average (trend / momentum).

Possible signal: trend-following effects (prices above their average tend to keep trending)
and mean reversion after stretched moves. Expressed as a ratio, so it is scale-free and
comparable between $10 and $100,000 prices (Phase 2: never feed raw price levels).

| feature | lookback | in sets | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `close_to_sma_20` | 19 | v1 | close / SMA(close, 20 days incl. today) - 1 |
| `close_to_sma_50` | 49 | v1 | close / SMA(close, 50 days incl. today) - 1 |

## range

Source: [`backend/src/marketlens/features/range.py`](../backend/src/marketlens/features/range.py)

Intraday range.

Possible signal: (high - low) / close is a one-day volatility estimate that also sees moves
which reverted before the close (the close-to-close return misses them). Range-based
estimators are known to be more efficient than close-to-close ones.

| feature | lookback | in sets | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `range_pct` | 0 | v1 | (high - low) / close of the day |

## returns

Source: [`backend/src/marketlens/features/returns.py`](../backend/src/marketlens/features/returns.py)

Past log returns.

Possible signal: short-term reversal or momentum. Phase 2 found daily return autocorrelation
is weak and fading (Ljung-Box p 0.000 → 0.094 across eras), so expect little on their own;
they matter mostly as inputs that interact with volatility.

| feature | lookback | in sets | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log_return_1d` | 1 | v1 | Log return over the last day: ln(close_t / close_t-1) |
| `log_return_30d` | 30 | v1 | Log return over the last 30 days: ln(close_t / close_t-30) |
| `log_return_7d` | 7 | v1 | Log return over the last 7 days: ln(close_t / close_t-7) |

## volatility

Source: [`backend/src/marketlens/features/volatility.py`](../backend/src/marketlens/features/volatility.py)

Realised volatility (std of daily log returns; not annualised).

Possible signal: the strongest structure Phase 2 found is volatility clustering (ACF of
|returns| 0.33 at lag 1, significant in every era). Recent volatility predicts the SIZE of
tomorrow's move, and the 7/30 ratio says whether the market is calming down or heating up
(a regime-change indicator).

| feature | lookback | in sets | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volatility_30d` | 30 | v1 | Std of daily log returns over the last 30 days |
| `volatility_7d` | 7 | v1 | Std of daily log returns over the last 7 days |
| `volatility_ratio_7_30` | 30 | v1 | volatility_7d / volatility_30d: >1 means volatility is rising versus the last month |

## volume

Source: [`backend/src/marketlens/features/volume.py`](../backend/src/marketlens/features/volume.py)

Trading activity.

Possible signal: unusual volume accompanies news, liquidations and regime changes, and often
precedes or confirms large moves. Volume is heavy-tailed and contains zero-volume days
(Phase 3 found 3 in Jan 2015), so we work on log(1 + volume), which is finite at zero.

| feature | lookback | in sets | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volume_change_1d` | 1 | v1 | log(1+volume_t) - log(1+volume_t-1) |
| `volume_zscore_30d` | 30 | v1 | z-score of log(1+volume) today versus the PREVIOUS 30 days (today excluded) |
